r7-hunt-preemption.title: HUNT: retirement-layout pre-emption test
r7-hunt-preemption.imperative: Independently test the Commander's candidate defect: does EPISODE_STORE.md's SS7/SS8 language pre-empt the held-open retirement layout decision by baking in Option B's (status-field) mechanics as the retrieval contract, forfeiting Option A's (directory-split) structural immunity? Also scan the worked example, field list, retrieval description, and README for any other quiet layout assumption.
r7-hunt-preemption.finding: Commander's reading is CORRECT, and independent testing found a sharper instance than the one flagged. (1) SS7 worked example states as unconditional fact: 'Nothing else in the file changes... The file is never deleted, moved, or truncated -- retained in history is one field flip on the same file at the same path, not a second data store to keep in sync.' That sentence is true ONLY under Option B; Option A's own definition two paragraphs later is 'moves the file between episodes/active/<id>.md and episodes/retired/<id>.md'. The worked example asserts Option B's behavior as settled fact before the HELD OPEN paragraph that follows it, which is a direct self-contradiction, not just an inference risk. (2) SS8's 'additive not a rewrite' claim does not hold as written: it specifies the enumerate-non-retired-episodes primitive as implemented by 'a line-anchored grep' (content-based, i.e. checking a status field), and SS7's single-line-enforcement paragraph confirms this is meant as the concrete mechanism ('a negative not-retired filter over Retirement's status field'). No membership-predicate seam is named anywhere in the doc analogous to SS1's own 'one named seam' treatment of durable_root(). If g3 is built literally to this text (grep-based), then ratifying Option A at g4 would require REWRITING g3's ordinary-search implementation from content-parsing to directory-globbing to realize any of Option A's structural-immunity benefit -- otherwise Option A becomes a cosmetic directory split that retrieval never actually trusts, which is precisely 'true in letter and hollow in effect.' So SS7's own claim that binding the layout later is 'additive, not a rewrite of g2 or g3's own contracts' is true only for the CALLER-FACING interface name, not for the implementation -- and the document does not make that distinction, so a builder reading it literally would not know to preserve rewrite-freedom. (3) The right fix (yes to Commander's Q3): route the membership predicate through one named adapter seam, mirroring this doc's own SS1 vocabulary (Seam/Adapter, cf. references/global-everyone.md 'Deep-module vocabulary') -- e.g. is_episode_active(episode_id) with an Option-B adapter (grep status field) and an Option-A adapter (check which directory the id resolves under); g3's enumerate/select primitives call the seam, never the mechanism directly. That makes g4's binding genuinely additive (swap the adapter behind the seam) instead of requiring a retrieval rewrite. (4) Other quiet-assumption sweep: SS2 states unconditionally 'The filename IS the id: episodes/<id>.md' -- under Option A this is false for the full relative path (it would be episodes/active/<id>.md or episodes/retired/<id>.md); basename-is-id would still hold but the doc does not make that distinction, a second minor instance of the same root cause. README.md and SS3/SS4/SS6 (field list, Stratum A table) do not encode a layout assumption -- checked and clean. CONCLUSION: this is a real, fixable defect confined to prose (SS2, SS7, SS8) -- no design re-litigation needed, but it must be fixed in THIS gate's own deliverable before g2/g3 build against it, not deferred, since the defect is that the contract text itself already leans on one option.
